text:
Sea's Digital Entertainment (Garena) revenue rose 26.1%, from US$1.9 billion in 2024 to US$2.4 billion (US$2,408.8 million) in 2025 [Sea, FY2025, p.100, F-3].

Key drivers:

1. **User growth and engagement**: Average Quarterly Active Users (QAUs) grew 5.7% (from 622.3 million in 2024 to 657.7 million in 2025), while average Quarterly Paying Users (QPUs) grew more sharply at 23.9% (from 50.5 million to 62.6 million) — indicating deepened paying user penetration (a larger share of the active base converting into paying users) [Sea, FY2025, p.100].

2. **Stronger bookings and deferred revenue recognition**: Bookings (GAAP revenue plus change in deferred revenue, used as a proxy for cash spent by users) were notably stronger in 2025, which also drove an increase in the change in deferred revenue on the cash flow statement, further corroborating the stronger user spending activity [Sea, FY2025, p.107].

3. **Higher gross profit tied to the same drivers**: Management explicitly attributes higher digital entertainment gross profits in 2025 to "increase in our active user base as well as deepened paying user penetration" [Sea, FY2025, p.107].

Note that cost of revenue for this segment also rose 29.6% (from US$610.6 million to US$791.4 million), driven by higher third-party payment channel costs (in line with the revenue increase) plus higher royalty payments to game developers and higher royalties for third-party intellectual property use [Sea, FY2025, p.100] — but this pertains to costs rather than the revenue increase itself.

In short, the increase in Garena revenue in FY2025 is explained primarily by growth in the active user base and a meaningfully deeper penetration of paying users (QPU growth far outpacing QAU growth), reflecting stronger monetization of the game player base and higher bookings during the year.
